category: Reaction Engineering, Chemistry, Reacting Flow & Thermodynamics
description: Ideal reactor models (batch, CSTR, semibatch, plug flow), reaction and species definitions, CHEMKIN import, surface reactions, population balances, reacting-flow multiphysics couplings, electrophoretic transport and the Thermodynamics property package of the Chemical Reaction Engineering Module. Java type strings were taken from COMSOL 6.4 Application Library models.

tools.name: Batch Reactor Types (Reaction Engineering)
tools.description: Reactor options Batch and Batch, constant volume of the Reaction Engineering interface: a closed, perfectly mixed system without inlet or outlet streams. Batch accounts for a variable reactor volume (gas-phase reactions at constant pressure), while Batch, constant volume is the default and fixes the volume Vr. Species balances dc/dt = R are solved in time, with an optional energy balance for nonisothermal operation.
tools.usage: Reaction Engineering > Reactor > Reactor type = Batch | Batch, constant volume; Java: model.component("comp1").physics("re").prop("reactor").set("reactor", "batchvol") (0D component: model.component().create("comp1", true); physics().create("re", "ReactionEng"))

parameters.name: reactor
parameters.description: batchvol (Batch, constant volume, default) or batch (variable volume).

parameters.name: Vr
parameters.description: Reactor volume.

parameters.name: prop("energybalance") energybalance
parameters.description: exclude (isothermal, set T) or include (solve for T with Qext heating/cooling).

parameters.name: Reactor pressure
parameters.description: Ideal gas law, constant, or user defined for gas-phase mixtures.

tools.notes: Use a Time Dependent study. The 'batch' option string for the variable-volume batch is inferred from naming; the Application Library models confirm batchvol, cstrvol, cstrmass, semibatch and plugflow.

tools.name: CSTR, Constant Volume / Constant Mass (Reaction Engineering)
tools.description: Continuous stirred tank reactor options of the Reaction Engineering interface, where species enter through Feed Inlet streams and leave with the outlet at the reactor composition. CSTR, constant volume keeps Vr fixed and adjusts the outlet rate; CSTR, constant mass/generic lets the volume change and either holds the total mass constant or uses a user-specified outlet flow. The volumetric production rate vp from reactions is computed automatically or given by the user.
tools.usage: Reaction Engineering > Reactor type = CSTR, constant volume | CSTR, constant mass/generic; Java: model.component("comp1").physics("re").prop("reactor").set("reactor", "cstrvol")

parameters.name: reactor
parameters.description: cstrvol or cstrmass.

parameters.name: Vr
parameters.description: Reactor volume (constant-volume CSTR) or initial volume.

parameters.name: vp / reactorparsource
parameters.description: Volumetric production rate, Automatic or UserDefined.

parameters.name: v
parameters.description: Volumetric outlet rate for the generic CSTR.

tools.notes: Add at least one Feed Inlet. Solve with a Time Dependent study; a steady state is reached by integrating long enough or with a Stationary study.

tools.name: Semibatch Reactor (Reaction Engineering)
tools.description: Reactor option in which reactants are added through one or more Feed Inlet streams but nothing leaves, so the reactor volume grows with the feed and the volumetric production rate. The energy balance is the same as for the CSTR types. Typical for polymerizations and fed-batch fermentations where feeding controls heat release or selectivity.
tools.usage: Reaction Engineering > Reactor type = Semibatch; Java: model.component("comp1").physics("re").prop("reactor").set("reactor", "semibatch")

parameters.name: reactor
parameters.description: semibatch.

parameters.name: vp
parameters.description: Volumetric production rate (Automatic from reactions or user defined).

parameters.name: Feed Inlet: vf, FeedSpeciesConcentration
parameters.description: Feed rate and composition, possibly time dependent.

tools.notes: Initial reactor volume is set in the Initial Values node (Vr0).

tools.name: Plug Flow Reactor (Reaction Engineering)
tools.description: Reactor option describing a tubular reactor with gradients only in the axial direction. Species molar flow rates F_i (mol/s) and temperature are solved as functions of the reactor volume rather than time, using the Stationary Plug Flow study step. Surface species are not allowed; the volumetric flow rate follows from the ideal gas law or is user defined, and external heating is given per reactor volume.
tools.usage: Reaction Engineering > Reactor type = Plug flow; Java: model.component("comp1").physics("re").prop("reactor").set("reactor", "plugflow")

parameters.name: reactor
parameters.description: plugflow.

parameters.name: v / vplug
parameters.description: Volumetric flow rate (Automatic from molar flows and pressure, or user defined).

parameters.name: Qextplug
parameters.description: External heating or cooling per reactor volume (W/m^3).

parameters.name: Initial Values: F0, T0plug
parameters.description: Inlet molar flow rates and inlet temperature.

tools.notes: Replace the Time Dependent step by Stationary Plug Flow when switching to this reactor type; combining Reaction Engineering with Stationary Plug Flow does not by itself set the reactor type.

tools.name: Stationary Plug Flow (study step)
tools.description: Study step for Reaction Engineering models using the Plug flow reactor type, solving the steady species molar flow rates and temperature along the reactor volume coordinate. The reactor volume range to integrate over is specified in the study step, analogous to the output times of a Time Dependent step. Batch, CSTR and semibatch reactors use Time Dependent instead.
tools.usage: Study > Stationary Plug Flow; Java: model.study("std1").create("spf", "StationaryPlugflow")

parameters.name: Reactor volume
parameters.description: Range of reactor volumes at which to store the solution, e.g. range(0,0.01,1)[m^3].

parameters.name: Tolerance
parameters.description: Relative tolerance of the underlying ODE solver.

tools.notes: Plot species molar flows re.F_<species> versus re.Vr in a 1D Plot Group with a Global plot.

tools.name: Reaction (Reaction Engineering)
tools.description: Node that defines one chemical reaction from a formula such as A + B <=> C. The arrow sets the type (<=> reversible, => irreversible, = equilibrium), participating Species nodes and stoichiometry are created automatically, and a Balance button can balance the equation. Rates follow the mass action law by default or a user-defined expression with explicit orders; rate constants can be constants or Arrhenius expressions with frequency factor, temperature exponent and activation energy.
tools.usage: Reaction Engineering (or Chemistry) > Reaction (rch1); Java: model.component("comp1").physics("re").create("rch1", "ReactionChem", -1)

parameters.name: formula
parameters.description: Reaction formula; rType becomes irrev, rev or equil.

parameters.name: ReactionExpression
parameters.description: Automatic (mass action law) or UserDefined rate r with forward/reverse orders.

parameters.name: kf, kr / setKeq0, Keq0
parameters.description: Rate constants, or forward constant plus equilibrium constant for reversible reactions.

parameters.name: useArrhenius, Af, nf, Ef (Ar, nr, Er)
parameters.description: Arrhenius parameters with Tref = 1 K.

parameters.name: H, S, Q
parameters.description: Enthalpy, entropy and heat source of reaction (Automatic from species thermodynamics).

tools.notes: Rate variables are re.r_1, re.kf_1 etc.; species rates re.R_<species>. The Chemistry interface uses the same node type without a reactor model.

tools.name: Mass Action Law and Arrhenius Kinetics (Reaction Engineering / Chemistry)
tools.description: Theory behind the default rate expressions: for reaction j, r_j = kf_j * prod(c_i^(-nu_ij)) over reactants minus kr_j * prod(c_i^(nu_ij)) over products, with stoichiometric coefficients negative for reactants. Rate constants can follow the extended Arrhenius law k = A*T^n*exp(-E/(Rg*T)), where the units of A depend on the reaction order. Surface reactions use surface concentrations and site densities in the same framework.
tools.usage: Reaction node > Reaction Rate = Mass action law; Rate Constants > Use Arrhenius expressions

parameters.name: A (Af, Ar)
parameters.description: Frequency factor, units (m^3/mol)^(alpha-1)/s for order alpha.

parameters.name: n (nf, nr)
parameters.description: Temperature exponent.

parameters.name: E (Ef, Er)
parameters.description: Activation energy (J/mol).

tools.example:
Application Library: Chemical_Reaction_Engineering_Module/Tutorials/activation_energy (estimating Arrhenius parameters from experimental data with parameter estimation).
r = kf*c_A*c_B with kf = Af*T^nf*exp(-Ef/(R_const*T)).
tools.notes: For non-elementary kinetics set Reaction Rate to User defined and specify the orders so that units of k are correct.

tools.name: Equilibrium Constant and Equilibrium Reactions (Reaction Engineering / Chemistry)
tools.description: Equilibrium reactions (formula with '=') are enforced algebraically: the equilibrium expression built from activities equals the equilibrium constant Keq0, and the interface picks dependent species to satisfy it. The constant can be entered directly or computed from the Gibbs free energy of reaction using species enthalpies and entropies. Reversible kinetic reactions can alternatively specify kf and Keq0 so that kr = kf/Keq0.
tools.usage: Reaction node with Reaction type = Equilibrium > Equilibrium Settings; Java: feature("rch2").set("formula", "OH-+H+=H2O"); set("Keq0", "Kequi_2")

parameters.name: Keq0
parameters.description: Equilibrium constant, User defined or Automatic from Gibbs energy (EqConstantFromGibbsEnergy).

parameters.name: Equilibrium expression
parameters.description: Automatic from stoichiometry and activities, or user defined.

parameters.name: Dependent species
parameters.description: Species solved from the equilibrium conditions (set on the interface).

tools.notes: Chemistry equilibrium reactions can be picked up by the Equilibrium Reaction node of Transport of Diluted Species.

tools.name: Species (Reaction Engineering)
tools.description: Node created automatically for each species in a reaction formula (or added manually) holding species-specific data. The type can be Bulk species (mol/m^3), Surface species (mol/m^2, named X_surf) or Solvent; chemical formula, molar mass and charge are deduced from the name. It also stores thermodynamic data (enthalpy, entropy, heat capacity or NASA polynomials), transport parameters (Lennard-Jones sigma, epsilon/kB, dipole moment) and the species rate expression.
tools.usage: Reaction Engineering > Species: <name>; Java type: "SpeciesChem" (tag equals the species name)

parameters.name: sType
parameters.description: volumetric (bulk), surface or solvent.

parameters.name: M, z
parameters.description: Molar mass and charge.

parameters.name: speciesEnthalpy, h, s, Cp
parameters.description: Thermodynamic properties (user defined, NASA format or from Thermodynamics).

parameters.name: sigma, epsilonkb, mu
parameters.description: Lennard-Jones parameters and dipole moment for transport properties.

parameters.name: rho
parameters.description: Species density for liquid mixture density.

tools.notes: Species names must follow the Valid Species Names rules (charges written as + and -, surface species with (ads)).

tools.name: Reversible Reaction Group (Reaction Engineering)
tools.description: Table-based node that holds many reversible reactions with their kinetic parameters in one place, typically populated by importing a CHEMKIN kinetics file. A coupled Species Group node is created with it, and with the energy balance included the enthalpy of reaction is computed from species thermodynamics. Tables can be saved to or loaded from text or Excel files.
tools.usage: Reaction Engineering > Reversible Reaction Group (rgr1); Java type: "ReversibleReactionGroup"

parameters.name: Reaction table
parameters.description: Reactants, products, Af, nf, Ef per reaction.

parameters.name: CHEMKIN import
parameters.description: Kinetics input file for the group.

parameters.name: Load from File / Save to File
parameters.description: Space-separated tables.

tools.example:
Application Library: Chemical_Reaction_Engineering_Module/Ideal_Tank_Reactors/compression_ignition (methane HCCI mechanism imported from CHEMKIN).
model.component("comp1").physics("re").create("rgr1", "ReversibleReactionGroup", -1);
tools.notes: Equilibrium Reaction Group is the analogous table for equilibrium reactions.

tools.name: Equilibrium Reaction Group (Reaction Engineering)
tools.description: Table node for entering a large number of equilibrium reactions with their equilibrium constants, analogous to the Reversible Reaction Group. A coupled Species Group is created automatically, and tables can be loaded from or saved to files. Useful for aqueous speciation networks.
tools.usage: Reaction Engineering > Equilibrium Reaction Group

parameters.name: Equilibrium reaction table
parameters.description: Reactants, products and equilibrium constant per reaction.

tools.example:
1. Right-click Reaction Engineering > Equilibrium Reaction Group.
2. Load a text file with columns reactants, products, Keq.
3. Set initial values of total components and solve with a Time Dependent or Stationary study.
tools.notes: Species in the group-generated Species Group come only from this reaction group.

tools.name: Species Group (Reaction Engineering)
tools.description: Node created automatically with a Reversible or Equilibrium Reaction Group that tabulates molecular-level data of its volumetric and surface species, typically from CHEMKIN transport files. It follows the enable/disable state of its reaction group and hosts the Species Thermodynamics and Species Activity subnodes.
tools.usage: Reaction Engineering > Species Group (sg_rgr1); Java type: "SpeciesGroup"

parameters.name: Property for Volumetric Species / Surface Species
parameters.description: Molar mass, Lennard-Jones parameters, dipole moment.

parameters.name: CHEMKIN transport import
parameters.description: Available when transport properties are calculated.

parameters.name: Show species name from CHEMKIN file
parameters.description: Adds the original CHEMKIN names as a column.

tools.example: Application Library: Chemical_Reaction_Engineering_Module/Reactors_with_Mass_and_Heat_Transfer/gaas_cvd (reaction groups with surface species).
tools.notes: Species Group exists only as a companion of a reaction group.

tools.name: Species Thermodynamics (Reaction Engineering)
tools.description: Subnode of Species Group, created when the energy balance is included, that defines enthalpies, entropies and heat capacities of all group species for mixture properties and heats of reaction. Data are given in NASA 7-coefficient polynomial format (typically imported from a CHEMKIN thermodynamic file) or as user-defined enthalpy and heat capacity.
tools.usage: Reaction Engineering > Species Group > Species Thermodynamics (sthm1); Java type: "SpeciesThermodynamics"

parameters.name: Type
parameters.description: NASA format or User defined.

parameters.name: NASA coefficients
parameters.description: a1..a7 for low and high temperature ranges with Tlo, Tmid, Thi.

parameters.name: CHEMKIN thermodynamic import
parameters.description: Browse and Import a thermo file (NASA format only).

tools.example: Application Library: Chemical_Reaction_Engineering_Module/Ideal_Tank_Reactors/compression_ignition.
tools.notes: Heat capacity Cp/R = a1 + a2*T + a3*T^2 + a4*T^3 + a5*T^4 in the NASA format.

tools.name: Species Activity (Reaction Engineering)
tools.description: Subnode of Species Group that creates activity variables for all species in the group, with editable activity coefficients for volumetric and surface species. It is generated automatically when Use activity is selected in the interface Activity section, so that rate and equilibrium expressions use activities instead of concentrations for nonideal mixtures.
tools.usage: Reaction Engineering > Species Group > Species Activity (enable Activity > Use activity on the interface)

parameters.name: Activity coefficient
parameters.description: Per species in the Species Activity and Surface Species Activity tables.

parameters.name: prop("Activity") useActivity, c0s, csurf0s
parameters.description: Interface switch and standard-state concentrations.

tools.example:
model.component("comp1").physics("re").prop("Activity").set("useActivity", "1");
model.component("comp1").physics("re").prop("Activity").set("c0s", "1000[mol/m^3]");
tools.notes: For single reactions (not groups) the activity coefficient is set on each Species node.

tools.name: Additional Source (Reaction Engineering)
tools.description: Adds extra rate terms (mol/(m^3*s) for bulk species, mol/(m^2*s) for surface species) and, for CSTR and semibatch reactors, an additional volumetric production rate to the reactor balances. Use it for sources not described by reactions, such as gas-liquid mass transfer or dosing terms.
tools.usage: Reaction Engineering > Additional Source (add1); Java type: "AdditionalSourceFeature"

parameters.name: AddR
parameters.description: Additional rate expression per volumetric species.

parameters.name: vp
parameters.description: Additional volumetric production rate (CSTR and semibatch).

parameters.name: Surface species rates
parameters.description: Additional surface species rates.

tools.notes: Additional sources are also exported by Generate Space-Dependent Model when applicable.

tools.name: Feed Inlet (Reaction Engineering)
tools.description: Adds an inlet stream to CSTR and semibatch reactors with a volumetric feed rate and the feed composition. With the energy balance included, the feed temperature and species enthalpies of the stream are also specified. Several Feed Inlet nodes can represent separate feeds.
tools.usage: Reaction Engineering > Feed Inlet (feed1); Java: model.component("comp1").physics("re").create("feed1", "FeedStream", -1)

parameters.name: vf
parameters.description: Volumetric feed rate (m^3/s).

parameters.name: FeedSpeciesConcentration
parameters.description: Concentration of each species in the feed.

parameters.name: Tf
parameters.description: Feed inlet temperature (energy balance included).

parameters.name: FeedSpeciesEnthalpy / enthalpyType
parameters.description: Species enthalpy from Species nodes or user defined.

tools.notes: Not available for batch or plug-flow reactor types.

tools.name: Initial Values (Reaction Engineering)
tools.description: Global node holding initial species concentrations (or inlet molar flows for plug flow), surface species coverages, the initial reactor volume and initial temperature. An optional pre-equilibration step can first bring equilibrium reactions to equilibrium from the given totals.
tools.usage: Reaction Engineering > Initial Values (inits1); Java type: "SpeciesInitialValue"

parameters.name: initialValue
parameters.description: Initial concentration per volumetric species.

parameters.name: F0
parameters.description: Inlet molar flow rates (plug flow).

parameters.name: Vr0, T0, T0plug
parameters.description: Initial reactor volume and temperature.

parameters.name: preEquilibrationEnabled
parameters.description: Pre-equilibrate equilibrium reactions before time stepping.

tools.notes: Species order in the tables follows the VolumetricSpecies list.

tools.name: Generate Space-Dependent Model (Reaction Engineering)
tools.description: Exports a validated 0D reaction model to a 1D, 2D or 3D component: it creates a Chemistry interface with the kinetics and mixture properties plus selected species transport, fluid flow and heat transfer interfaces, a study, and multiphysics couplings such as Reacting Flow, Diluted Species. Pressing Create/Refresh builds or updates the space-dependent model; only one such node is allowed per interface.
tools.usage: Reaction Engineering toolbar > Generate Space-Dependent Model (sync1) > Create/Refresh; Java type: "ReactionToMph"

parameters.name: geomToUse
parameters.description: Component to use (new 1D/2D/3D or existing).

parameters.name: massbalance
parameters.description: Species transport interface to create, e.g. tds or tcs.

parameters.name: momentumbalance / energybalance
parameters.description: Fluid flow and heat transfer interfaces (or none).

parameters.name: study
parameters.description: Study type to create, e.g. Stationary or Time Dependent.

tools.notes: The generated geometry is empty; build geometry, boundary conditions and mesh in the new component afterwards.

tools.name: CHEMKIN Import (Reaction Engineering / Chemistry)
tools.description: Import of CHEMKIN input files for gas-phase kinetics (into a Reversible Reaction Group), thermodynamic data in NASA polynomial format (Species Thermodynamics) and transport data (Species Group). The files can be read independently, all imported values stay editable, and the data are used both for ideal reactors and for space-dependent models via Generate Space-Dependent Model.
tools.usage: Reaction Engineering > CHEMKIN Import for Species Properties / Reversible Reaction Group > CHEMKIN section > Browse > Import; interface prop("chemkin")

parameters.name: Kinetics file
parameters.description: Reactions with A, n, E (imported into a Reversible Reaction Group).

parameters.name: Thermo file
parameters.description: NASA 7-coefficient polynomials for Cp, h, s.

parameters.name: Transport file
parameters.description: Lennard-Jones parameters, dipole moment, polarizability.

tools.example: Application Library: Chemical_Reaction_Engineering_Module/Ideal_Tank_Reactors/compression_ignition and Reactors_with_Mass_and_Heat_Transfer/gaas_cvd; Tutorials/nonisothermal_plug_flow imports only a thermodynamic file.
tools.notes: When CHEMKIN files are imported the interface cannot be coupled to a Thermodynamics system.

tools.name: Mixture Properties and Species Matching (Chemistry)
tools.description: Interface-level settings of the Chemistry interface that define whether the mixture is Diluted or Concentrated species, its phase (gas or liquid), density model and optional coupling to a Thermodynamic System. The Species Matching table maps Chemistry species to the concentrations or mass fractions solved by a transport interface so that reaction rates, heat sources and transport properties are evaluated with the local composition. Calculate Transport Properties generates diffusivities, viscosity and conductivity.
tools.usage: Chemistry > Mixture Properties / Species Matching / Calculate Transport Properties; Java: model.component("comp1").physics("chem").prop("mixture").set("mixture", "gas")

parameters.name: ConcentrationType
parameters.description: Diluted species (molar concentrations) or MassFraction (concentrated).

parameters.name: mixture
parameters.description: gas or liquid.

parameters.name: Thermodynamics / PropertyPackage
parameters.description: Couple to a Thermodynamic System for properties.

parameters.name: prop("ChemistryModelInputParameter") MassTransfer, ConcentrationInput
parameters.description: Species matching to a transport interface (e.g. tcs with wH2, wHCl...).

parameters.name: prop("calcTransport") calcTransport
parameters.description: Compute mixture transport properties.

tools.notes: The Chemistry interface solves no equations itself; it only defines variables used by the transport interfaces through Reactions/Reaction Sources nodes.

tools.name: Electrode Reaction / Electrode Reaction Group (Chemistry)
tools.description: Chemistry nodes, available with an electrochemistry module, that define a charge-transfer reaction written as a reduction with 'e' for electrons (for example O2+4e<=>2O(ads)). The equilibrium potential is computed from the Nernst equation with reference concentrations, or automatically from species enthalpies and entropies, and kinetics variables can be used by Electrode Reaction nodes of current-distribution interfaces. An Electrode Reaction Group collects all reactions on one electrode and sums their currents.
tools.usage: Chemistry > Electrode Reaction (er1) / Electrode Reaction Group; Java type: "ElectrodeReactionChem"

parameters.name: Formula
parameters.description: Reduction reaction with 'e' and '<=>', phases (aq), (s), (g) optional.

parameters.name: Equilibrium potential
parameters.description: Nernst equation with reference electrode potential, Automatic from thermodynamics, or user defined.

parameters.name: Reference Concentrations
parameters.description: Reference states used in the reaction quotient.

parameters.name: Electrode kinetics
parameters.description: Exchange current density and transfer coefficients for use in current distribution interfaces.

tools.example:
Application Library: Fuel_Cell_and_Electrolyzer_Module/Electrolyzers/soec_thermodynamics (Chemistry electrode reactions coupled to a Secondary Current Distribution SOEC model).
model.component("comp1").physics("chem").create("er1", "ElectrodeReactionChem", 3);
tools.notes: Requires the Battery Design, Corrosion, Electrochemistry, Electrodeposition or Fuel Cell & Electrolyzer Module in addition to Chemistry.

tools.name: Surface Reactions (sr)
tools.description: Boundary-level interface solving for surface (adsorbed) species concentrations in mol/m^2 and immobile bulk deposit species on reacting boundaries. Surface species can diffuse tangentially by Fick's law; site density and site occupancy numbers define coverage, and bulk species growth gives deposit thickness. It is combined with a domain transport interface whose Surface Reactions boundary node supplies gas-phase fluxes.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Chemical Species Transport > Surface Reactions; Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("sr", "SurfaceReactions", "geom1")

parameters.name: Number of surface species / bulk species
parameters.description: Dependent variables cs1.. and cb1..

parameters.name: Surface Properties
parameters.description: Site density Gamma, occupancy Sigma, surface diffusion, bulk molar mass and density.

parameters.name: Reactions
parameters.description: Rates Rs for surface species and Rb for bulk species.

tools.notes: Surface Properties can compensate for boundary stretching on deforming geometries.

tools.name: Surface Properties (Surface Reactions)
tools.description: Default node of the Surface Reactions interface defining the density of sites Gamma_s (default 2e-5 mol/m^2), the site occupancy number of each surface species, surface diffusion coefficients and molar mass and density of bulk deposit species. It also contains the option to compensate for boundary stretching on deforming geometries.
tools.usage: Physics > Surface Reactions > Surface Properties (sp1); Java type: "SurfaceProperties"

parameters.name: Gamma
parameters.description: Density of sites (mol/m^2).

parameters.name: Sigma
parameters.description: Site occupancy number per surface species.

parameters.name: Surface diffusion
parameters.description: Isotropic/diagonal/symmetric/full diffusion tensor for surface species.

parameters.name: Bulk species M_i, rho_i
parameters.description: Used to compute deposit growth rate.

parameters.name: CompensateBoundaryStretching
parameters.description: Species conservation on deforming geometry.

tools.example:
Application Library: Chemical_Reaction_Engineering_Module/Reactors_with_Mass_Transfer/TiN_cvd_reactor.
model.component("comp1").physics("sr").feature("sp1").set("Gamma", "2e-5[mol/m^2]");
tools.notes: Coverage fraction theta = Sigma*cs/Gamma.

tools.name: Reactions (Surface Reactions)
tools.description: Node adding reaction rate expressions Rs (mol/(m^2*s)) for each surface species and Rb for each bulk (deposited) species on the selected boundaries. Rates typically come from a Chemistry interface with surface reactions or are written in terms of surface and gas concentrations.
tools.usage: Physics > Surface Reactions > Reactions (reac1); Java type: "Reactions"

parameters.name: Rs_<cs>
parameters.description: Reaction rate for each surface species.

parameters.name: Rb_<cb>
parameters.description: Reaction rate for each bulk species.

tools.example:
Application Library: Chemical_Reaction_Engineering_Module/Reactors_with_Mass_Transfer/TiN_cvd_reactor.
model.component("comp1").physics("sr").feature("reac1").set("Rs_cTiN", "k_dep*cTiCl4");
tools.notes: Surface Concentration can fix surface species values on edges/points.

tools.name: Size-Based Population Balance (pbsb)
tools.description: Interface for the size distribution of particles, droplets or bubbles, solving the discretized population number density n (1/m^4) of each size interval (at least five). It supports nucleation, growth, dissolution, aggregation and breakage and, in 1D-3D, transport by convection and diffusion. It works in 0D for well-mixed crystallizers as well as in space-dependent models.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Chemical Species Transport > Precipitation and Crystallization > Size-Based Population Balance; Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("pbsb", "PopulationBalanceSizeBased", "geom1")

parameters.name: Size discretization
parameters.description: Number and range of size intervals.

parameters.name: Growth kinetics
parameters.description: Nucleation model (e.g. HomogeneousBiIonic) and growth rate model (e.g. TransportControlled).

parameters.name: Fluid
parameters.description: Velocity and diffusivity for space-dependent transport.

parameters.name: Inflow / Outflow / Number Density
parameters.description: Boundary conditions for the distribution.

tools.example:
Application Library: Chemical_Reaction_Engineering_Module/Mixing_and_Separation/barium_sulfate_precipitation, turbulent_aggregation and cooling_crystallization_optimization.
model.component("comp1").physics().create("pbsb", "PopulationBalanceSizeBased", "geom1");
tools.notes: Use the Precipitation multiphysics couplings to link supersaturation from a species transport interface.

tools.name: Precipitation and Crystallization (multiphysics interfaces)
tools.description: Predefined multiphysics interfaces that combine the mass balance of dissolved species with the Size-Based Population Balance of the precipitate, and for space-dependent models also the flow of the solution. The Precipitation (global) and Precipitation in Fluid Flow couplings pass the precipitating species concentration, equilibrium solubility, diffusivity and molar mass between interfaces so nucleation and growth consume solute.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Chemical Species Transport > Precipitation and Crystallization > Precipitation and Crystallization (in Fluid Flow); coupling Java: model.component("comp1").multiphysics().create("pff1", "PrecipitationInFluidFlow", 3)

parameters.name: cspecies / cstar_species
parameters.description: Concentration of the precipitating species and its equilibrium (saturation) concentration.

parameters.name: Dspecies
parameters.description: Diffusivity used for transport-controlled growth.

parameters.name: precipitatingSpeciesMolarMass
parameters.description: Molar mass of the solid.

parameters.name: Fluid_physics / Species_physics / PopulationBalance_physics
parameters.description: Coupled interfaces (spf, tds, pbsb).

tools.notes: The 0D/global coupling type is "PrecipitationInFluidFlowGlobal" (label Precipitation).

tools.name: Reacting Flow, Diluted Species (multiphysics coupling)
tools.description: Multiphysics interface and coupling node (rfd) that combines Laminar Flow (or Brinkman Equations or a turbulent flow interface) with Transport of Diluted Species. The coupling synchronizes the velocity field and, for turbulent flow, adds turbulent mass diffusivity from a turbulent Schmidt number (Kays-Crawford model) and mass-transport wall functions.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Chemical Species Transport > Reacting Flow > Laminar Flow, Diluted Species; coupling Java: model.component("comp1").multiphysics().create("rfd1", "ReactingFlowDS", 3)

parameters.name: Fluid_physics / Species_physics
parameters.description: Coupled flow (spf, br) and transport (tds) interfaces.

parameters.name: MassTurbType / ScT
parameters.description: Turbulent mass transport model (KaysCrawford or user Schmidt number, default 0.71).

tools.notes: For concentrated mixtures the Reacting Flow coupling (NonIsothermalReactingFlow type) also passes density and the Stefan velocity.

tools.name: Reacting Flow in Porous Media / Porous Catalysts / Packed Beds (multiphysics interfaces)
tools.description: Group of predefined multiphysics interfaces that couple Brinkman Equations (free and porous flow) with diluted or concentrated species transport in porous media, porous catalysts, packed beds (including shrinking-core and moving-bed variants). The Reacting Flow or Reacting Flow, Diluted Species coupling passes velocity, and for concentrated species also density and mass sources, between the interfaces.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Chemical Species Transport > Reacting Flow in Porous Media > e.g. Transport of Diluted Species / Packed Beds, Transport of Concentrated Species

parameters.name: Flow interface
parameters.description: Brinkman Equations (br) or Free and Porous Media Flow.

parameters.name: Transport interface
parameters.description: TDS/TCS in porous media, porous catalysts or packed beds.

parameters.name: Coupling
parameters.description: Reacting Flow, Diluted Species (rfd) or Reacting Flow (nirf).

tools.example:
Application Library: Chemical_Reaction_Engineering_Module/Reactors_with_Porous_Catalysts/porous_reactor and steam_reformer.
1. Model Wizard > Reacting Flow in Porous Media > Transport of Diluted Species.
2. Assign a Porous Material to the catalyst bed.
3. Add reactions from a Chemistry interface and solve Stationary.
tools.notes: Add Heat Transfer in Porous Media for nonisothermal beds.

tools.name: Nonisothermal Reacting Flow (Reacting Flow coupling, laminar and turbulent)
tools.description: Multiphysics interfaces that add Chemistry, Transport of Concentrated Species, a laminar or turbulent flow interface (k-epsilon, k-omega, SST, low-Re k-epsilon, LES) and Heat Transfer in Fluids, joined by the Reacting Flow coupling. The coupling passes velocity, pressure, density, temperature and heat of reaction, and adds turbulent mass and heat transport (turbulent Schmidt and Prandtl numbers), wall functions and viscous dissipation.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Chemical Species Transport > Nonisothermal Reacting Flow > Laminar Flow | Turbulent Flow, k-epsilon ...; coupling Java: model.component("comp1").multiphysics().create("nirf1", "NonIsothermalReactingFlow", 3)

parameters.name: Fluid_physics / Species_physics / Chemistry_physics / Heat_physics
parameters.description: Coupled interfaces (spf, tcs, chem, ht).

parameters.name: MassTurbType, ScT
parameters.description: Turbulent mass transport model.

parameters.name: ThermalTurbModel, Prt
parameters.description: Turbulent heat transport model.

parameters.name: includeViscousDissipation
parameters.description: Viscous heating term.

tools.notes: Label in the Model Builder is 'Reacting Flow'. The Chemical Reaction Engineering Module is required; turbulence models need the CFD Module license for some variants.

tools.name: Dispersed Two-Phase Flow with Species Transport (multiphysics interface)
tools.description: Predefined multiphysics interface coupling a Mixture Model flow with Continuous Phase and Dispersed Phase Transport of Diluted Species interfaces. The Dispersed Two-Phase Flow, Diluted Species coupling provides phase velocities and volume fractions and interphase mass transfer of selected species through a mass transfer coefficient and partition coefficient. Used for liquid-liquid extraction and bubble columns.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Chemical Species Transport > Dispersed Two-Phase Flow with Species Transport > Laminar Flow; coupling Java: model.component("comp1").multiphysics().create("dds1", "DispersedTwoPhaseFlowDS", 2)

parameters.name: Fluid_physics
parameters.description: Mixture model interface (mm).

parameters.name: ContinuousPhaseSpecies_physics / DispersedPhaseSpecies_physics
parameters.description: The two TDS interfaces.

parameters.name: phaseTransferredSpecies, km, Kp
parameters.description: Species transferred between phases, mass transfer coefficient and partition coefficient.

tools.notes: Physics types of the species interfaces are DilutedSpeciesInContinuousPhase and DilutedSpeciesInDispersedPhase.

tools.name: Vapor-Liquid Equilibrium (multiphysics interfaces)
tools.description: Predefined interfaces that combine a fluid flow interface (laminar vapor flow, laminar two-phase flow, or turbulent k-epsilon, k-omega, SST, low-Re k-epsilon) with Transport of Concentrated Species in Vapor through a Reacting Flow coupling. They model evaporation and condensation of gas mixtures in contact with liquids, with vapor pressure from Thermodynamics.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Chemical Species Transport > Vapor-Liquid Equilibrium > Laminar Vapor Flow | Laminar Two-Phase Flow | Turbulent Flow ...

parameters.name: Vapor Inflow
parameters.description: Inlet composition from an upstream liquid.

parameters.name: Vapor-Liquid Interface / Vapor-Liquid-Solution Interface
parameters.description: Evaporation boundary conditions.

parameters.name: Thermodynamic System
parameters.description: Vapor pressure and activity model for the liquid.

tools.example: Application Library: Chemical_Reaction_Engineering_Module/Thermodynamics/droplet_evaporation_water_acetone (Laminar Two-Phase Flow with moving interface).
tools.notes: Couple heat transfer to include latent heat of evaporation.

tools.name: Electrophoretic Transport (el)
tools.description: Interface for electrophoretic transport of any number of species in water-based systems under potential gradients, based on Nernst-Planck transport with electroneutrality. Species can be strong and weak acids and bases, ampholytes, proteins and uncharged species, with water self-ionization handled by the Solvent node. It simulates zone electrophoresis, isotachophoresis, isoelectric focusing and moving boundary electrophoresis; immobile charged species represent gels.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Chemical Species Transport > Electrophoretic Transport (el); Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("el", "ElectrophoreticTransport", "geom1")

parameters.name: prop("TransportMechanism") Convection / MassTransferInPorousMedia
parameters.description: Additional transport mechanisms.

parameters.name: Species nodes
parameters.description: Fully Dissociated, Weak Acid, Weak Base, Ampholyte, Protein, Uncharged Species.

parameters.name: Boundary conditions
parameters.description: Potential, Current Density, Current, Insulation, Concentration, Inflow, Outflow.

tools.notes: Dependent variables are the electrolyte potential and the concentration of each species added by its species node.

tools.name: Weak Acid / Weak Base / Ampholyte / Protein (Electrophoretic Transport)
tools.description: Species nodes of the Electrophoretic Transport interface. Weak Acid and Weak Base support monoprotic or polyprotic dissociation with given pKa values; Ampholyte describes species whose average charge depends on pH via equilibrium constants (with base charge Z0) or an average-charge function; Protein is an ampholyte with defaults suited to macromolecules. Mobilities follow the Debye-Hueckel-Henry relation or user input.
tools.usage: Physics > Electrophoretic Transport > Weak Acid (wa1) / Weak Base (wb1) / Ampholyte (amph1) / Protein (prot1); Java types: "WeakAcid", "WeakBase", "Ampholyte", "Protein"

parameters.name: Number of dissociation steps
parameters.description: Monoprotic or polyprotic (weak acids/bases).

parameters.name: pKa values
parameters.description: Equilibrium constants per dissociation step.

parameters.name: Dissociation model (Ampholyte/Protein)
parameters.description: Equilibrium constants with base charge Z0, or Average charge as a function of pH.

parameters.name: Diffusion and migration
parameters.description: Diffusivity and mobility (Nernst-Einstein or Debye-Hueckel-Henry).

tools.example:
Application Library: Chemical_Reaction_Engineering_Module/Electrokinetic_Effects/isoelectric_separation (proteins separated in a pH gradient).
model.component("comp1").physics("el").create("prot1", "Protein", 2);
tools.notes: The Solvent node defines H+ and OH- automatically; do not add them as separate species.

tools.name: Solvent (Electrophoretic Transport)
tools.description: Domain node defining the aqueous solvent: velocity field when convection is on, dynamic viscosity and relative permittivity (used in Debye-Hueckel-Henry mobilities), and the water self-ionization constant pKw. It automatically defines proton and hydroxide concentrations el.cH and el.cOH and their fluxes.
tools.usage: Physics > Electrophoretic Transport > Solvent (sol1); Java type: "Solvent"

parameters.name: Velocity field
parameters.description: User defined or from a flow interface.

parameters.name: Dynamic viscosity, Relative permittivity
parameters.description: Built-in water values by default.

parameters.name: pKw
parameters.description: Water self-ionization constant (built in or user defined).

tools.example: Application Library: Chemical_Reaction_Engineering_Module/Electrokinetic_Effects/zone_electrophoresis.
tools.notes: A Porous Matrix Properties node can model gels or porous media.

tools.name: Thermodynamic System (Thermodynamics)
tools.description: Global Definitions node created by the Thermodynamic System Wizard (select system phases, species from the built-in database, and thermodynamic model) that defines property functions for pure species, mixtures and phase equilibria. Systems can be Gas, Liquid, Vapor-liquid, Vapor-liquid-liquid or Liquid-liquid; species are found by name, CAS number or formula. Reaction Engineering and Chemistry interfaces can couple to it for all mixture properties.
tools.usage: Global Definitions > Thermodynamics > Thermodynamic System (wizard: Select System > Select Species > Select Thermodynamic Model); also from the Reaction Engineering/Chemistry toolbar

parameters.name: System
parameters.description: Gas, Liquid, Vapor-liquid, Vapor-liquid-liquid, Liquid-liquid.

parameters.name: Species
parameters.description: From the COMSOL database or User-Defined Species.

parameters.name: Thermodynamic model
parameters.description: Gas phase EOS and liquid phase activity model.

tools.example:
Application Library: Chemical_Reaction_Engineering_Module/Thermodynamics/engine_coolant_properties and distillation_column.
1. Right-click Global Definitions > Thermodynamics > Thermodynamic System.
2. Choose Vapor-liquid, add water and ethylene glycol, select NRTL for the liquid.
3. Right-click the system > Mixture Property to create density and heat capacity functions.
tools.notes: Systems can be exported to and imported from xml files (definition only, not generated functions) for reuse or to edit species data. Predefined System gives Dry air, Moist air or Water-steam directly.

tools.name: External Thermodynamic System (CAPE-OPEN)
tools.description: Thermodynamics node that takes species properties, mixture properties and phase-equilibrium calculations from an installed CAPE-OPEN compliant package (Thermo 1.0 or 1.1), such as COCO/TEA, Multiflash, VMGThermo, Simulis Thermodynamics or Aspen Properties. After installation the packages appear in the Thermodynamic System Wizard.
tools.usage: Global Definitions > Thermodynamics > External Thermodynamic System > select property package

parameters.name: Property package
parameters.description: Installed CAPE-OPEN package or template.

parameters.name: Species / phases
parameters.description: Defined by the external package; label reflects the included phases.

tools.example:
1. Install COCO and create a TEA property package template with the required compounds.
2. In COMSOL add Thermodynamics > External Thermodynamic System and pick the package.
3. Add Species Property or Equilibrium Calculation functions and use them in physics interfaces.
tools.notes: Calculations are delegated to the external software, so it must be installed on every machine (and cluster node) that solves the model.

tools.name: Predefined System (Thermodynamics)
tools.description: Shortcut that creates a thermodynamic system with all settings entered for Dry air, Moist air or Water-steam using the built-in database. Property functions, Generate Material and Equilibrium Calculation work as for other systems.
tools.usage: Global Definitions > Thermodynamics > Predefined System > Dry air | Moist air | Water-steam

parameters.name: System
parameters.description: Dry air, Moist air or Water-steam.

tools.example:
1. Add Thermodynamics > Predefined System > Moist air.
2. Right-click it > Generate Material to create a humid-air material for Laminar Flow and Heat Transfer.
tools.notes: Generate Material skips the phase selection for Dry Air and Moist Air.

tools.name: Species Property / Mixture Property (Thermodynamics)
tools.description: Wizards under a thermodynamic system that create property functions: Species Property gives pure-species parameters (molar mass, Lennard-Jones diameter, dipole moment) and functions of T or T and p (density, enthalpy, heat capacity, viscosity); Mixture Property gives functions of composition, temperature and pressure (density, enthalpy, heat capacity, surface tension for two-phase systems) with automatic derivatives.
tools.usage: Thermodynamic System > right-click > Species Property | Mixture Property (wizard: Select Properties > Select Phase > Select Species > Overview)

parameters.name: Amount base unit
parameters.description: mol or kg.

parameters.name: Phase
parameters.description: One of the system phases (two-phase for surface tension).

parameters.name: Species composition base unit
parameters.description: Mole fraction or Mass fraction (mixture properties).

tools.example:
Application Library: Chemical_Reaction_Engineering_Module/Thermodynamics/engine_coolant_properties.
Call the generated function in a material, e.g. rho = pp1_Density(T, p, x_water, x_glycol).
tools.notes: First-order T and p derivatives are defined automatically, second order for density and molar volume.

tools.name: Equilibrium Calculation (Thermodynamics)
tools.description: Wizard that creates functions for phase-equilibrium (flash) calculations of a thermodynamic system: bubble and dew points at given T or p, equilibrium at given (p,T), (p,H), (p,S) or (U,V). It generates phase-existence, phase-amount and phase-composition functions, and can produce phase envelopes for any number of species.
tools.usage: Thermodynamic System > right-click > Equilibrium Calculation (wizard: Select species > Equilibrium Specifications > Overview)

parameters.name: Equilibrium conditions
parameters.description: Temperature-pressure, pressure-enthalpy, pressure-entropy, internal energy-volume, bubble/dew point.

parameters.name: Phases
parameters.description: Phases included in the equilibrium.

parameters.name: Output functions
parameters.description: Exist, amount and composition functions per phase.

tools.example: Application Library: Chemical_Reaction_Engineering_Module/Thermodynamics/phase_envelope and distillation_column.
tools.notes: Equilibrium functions can be called from physics interfaces, e.g. to set equilibrium mole fractions at a vapor-liquid boundary.

tools.name: Generate Chemistry / Generate Material (Thermodynamics)
tools.description: Wizards that turn a thermodynamic system into model objects. Generate Chemistry creates a Chemistry interface populated with the selected species, fully coupled to the thermodynamics so mixture density and enthalpy come from property functions. Generate Material creates a Material node with density, heat capacity, thermal conductivity, viscosity and related properties for a chosen phase and composition.
tools.usage: Thermodynamic System > right-click > Generate Chemistry | Generate Material

parameters.name: Species / Name in Chemistry
parameters.description: Species to include and their names in Chemistry.

parameters.name: Component / Mass transfer
parameters.description: Target component and mixture type (diluted or concentrated).

parameters.name: Phase / Properties / Composition
parameters.description: For Generate Material: phase, properties and fixed composition.

tools.example:
1. Create a Gas thermodynamic system with CH4, H2O, CO, CO2, H2.
2. Generate Chemistry into comp1 with Mass transfer = Concentrated species.
3. Add reactions to the generated Chemistry and couple to Transport of Concentrated Species.
tools.notes: Generated materials are functions of the model inputs (T, p), so they update automatically with the solved temperature.

tools.name: Thermodynamic Models (Peng-Robinson, SRK, NRTL, UNIQUAC, UNIFAC...)
tools.description: Models available in the built-in thermodynamic property database. Equations of state: Ideal Gas Law, Peng-Robinson, Peng-Robinson (Twu), Soave-Redlich-Kwong, SRK (Graboski-Daubert) and Water (IAPWS). Liquid activity-coefficient models: Ideal Solution, Regular Solution, Extended Regular Solution, Wilson, NRTL, UNIQUAC, UNIFAC and Chao-Seader (Grayson-Streed). A decision tree in the documentation guides the choice based on components, pressure and data availability.
tools.usage: Thermodynamic System Wizard > Select Thermodynamic Model

parameters.name: Gas phase model
parameters.description: Ideal gas or cubic EOS for pressure-volume-temperature behaviour.

parameters.name: Liquid phase model
parameters.description: Activity coefficient model for nonideal liquid mixtures at low to moderate pressure.

tools.example: Vapor-liquid system of ethanol and water at 1 atm: Ideal Gas for the vapor, NRTL (or UNIFAC if interaction parameters are missing) for the liquid.
tools.notes: Cubic EOS models also describe liquids at high pressure; activity models are preferred for polar liquids at low pressure.
